notes: The projection carries two ἔτι tokens where the ASV writes 'yet' once. The word is given to the fronted Ἔτι, which stands in every reading, and the doubled s007 is `unrepresented` with SBLGNT.ROM.5.6.v004 (underdetermined, r00-base against r01) named in its note (rule 97's mirror case). Giving 'yet' to s007 instead remains defensible and the note says so.
ὄντων is a genitive absolute whose subject ἡμῶν is expressed, so ἡμῶν takes 'we' and the participle keeps only the supplied subordinator and copula (rule 74).
ἀσεβῶν → 'the ungodly' is an anarthrous substantival adjective; the supplied determiner is a rule 7 helper and the head stays on the adjective (rules 51 and 58).
A reference comparison will report the `unrepresented` second ἔτι as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.
